nodes.title: Security: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Security. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A router has 'hostname R1', 'ip domain-name corp.local', a 2048-bit RSA key pair?
flashcards.back: By default, VTY lines accept Telnet (transport input telnet) or nothing. Even with SSH fully configured on the device, the VTY lines must explicitly allow SSH with 'transport input ssh' (or 'transport input all'). Without this, the SSH daemon rejects inbound connections at the VTY level.

flashcards.front: DHCP snooping is configured. Which ports should be set as 'trusted'?
flashcards.back: Only ports connected to the real DHCP server or switch uplinks should be trusted. Untrusted ports (user devices) that send DHCP Offers are blocked, preventing rogue DHCP servers.

flashcards.front: Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) uses which database to validate ARP packets?
flashcards.back: DAI cross-references incoming ARP packets against the DHCP snooping binding table (IP-to-MAC mappings). Invalid ARPs — signs of ARP spoofing — are dropped.

flashcards.front: A security engineer discovers attackers are performing VLAN hopping via double-t?
flashcards.back: Double-tagging attacks work because the switch strips the outer tag (which matches the native VLAN) and forwards the frame with the inner tag onto a different VLAN. Changing the native VLAN from 1 to 999 only helps if no attacker is on VLAN 999. If any access port is assigned to VLAN 999, an attacker on that port can still perform double-tagging. The native VLAN must be an unused, dedicated VLAN with no access ports assigned to it. if any user port is in VLAN 999, that user can still double-tag frames targeting the new native VLAN

nodes.title: Routing: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Routing. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A router has these routes: 10.0.0.0/8, 10.1.0.0/16, and 10.1.1.0/24. A packet ar?
flashcards.back: Routers use longest prefix match. /24 is the most specific (longest) match for 10.1.1.5, so it wins over /16 and /8.

flashcards.front: What administrative distance does OSPF use by default?
flashcards.back: OSPF has an AD of 110. EIGRP internal is 90, RIP is 120, and EBGP is 20. Lower AD = more trusted.

flashcards.front: A floating static route is configured with AD 254. Under what condition does it ?
flashcards.back: A floating static route's AD is deliberately set higher than the primary protocol. It only enters the routing table when the primary route (with lower AD) is gone, acting as a backup.

flashcards.front: What does a router do when no route matches a packet's destination and no defaul?
flashcards.back: Without a matching route or default route, the router drops the packet and typically sends an ICMP Type 3 (Destination Unreachable) message back to the source.

nodes.title: Stp: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Stp. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: STP is enabled on a switch. A port is currently in the Listening state. What doe?
flashcards.back: In the Listening state, a port processes BPDUs to participate in the STP election, but does NOT forward frames or learn MAC addresses. Learning comes next, then Forwarding.

flashcards.front: PortFast is enabled on a switch port. What is a risk if PortFast is used incorre?
flashcards.back: PortFast skips STP Listening and Learning states. If another switch is connected, it bypasses the topology checks that prevent loops. Always pair PortFast with BPDU Guard on edge ports.

flashcards.front: BPDU Guard is enabled on a PortFast port. What happens when a BPDU is received?
flashcards.back: BPDU Guard immediately shuts down (err-disables) any PortFast port that receives a BPDU. This prevents unauthorized switches from being plugged into edge ports.

flashcards.front: RSTP (Rapid STP) introduced which port roles not present in classic STP?
flashcards.back: RSTP adds Alternate (discarding backup for the Root port) and Backup (discarding backup for the Designated port) roles, enabling much faster convergence than classic STP.

nodes.title: OSPF: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on OSPF. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: On a multi-access Ethernet segment, what is the OSPF Designated Router's primary?
flashcards.back: The DR collects LSAs from all neighbors and floods them to the segment, preventing every router from forming full adjacencies with every other router (N² problem).

flashcards.front: What is the OSPF Hello interval on a broadcast network by default?
flashcards.back: OSPF sends Hello packets every 10 seconds on broadcast/point-to-point links. On NBMA links the default is 30 seconds. The Dead interval is 4× the Hello interval.

flashcards.front: Which command shows OSPF neighbor state on a Cisco router?
flashcards.back: 'show ip ospf neighbor' lists all OSPF neighbors, their state (FULL, 2WAY, etc.), router IDs, and interfaces. FULL state means a complete adjacency has formed.

flashcards.front: Which command configures an OSPF process and assigns area 0 to an interface?
flashcards.back: Under 'router ospf 1', the 'network' command uses the network address + wildcard mask + area number. Alternatively, 'ip ospf 1 area 0' can be configured directly on the interface.

pairs.prompt: On a multi-access Ethernet segment, what is the OSPF Designa
pairs.answer: Reduces LSA flooding by acting as the central exchange point

nodes.title: Troubleshooting: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Troubleshooting. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An engineer runs 'show interfaces GigabitEthernet0/0' and sees: 'GigabitEthernet?
flashcards.back: 'Up/down' means the physical layer is working (carrier detected) but the data link layer cannot establish. Common causes: encapsulation mismatch (e.g., HDLC vs PPP), missing 'clock rate' on a DCE serial interface, or keepalive failures. 'Administratively down/down' would indicate a manual shutdown. likely due to keepalive failure, encapsulation mismatch, or missing clock rate on a serial link

flashcards.front: A router shows 'GigabitEthernet0/0 up/up' in 'show ip interface brief' and has a?
flashcards.back: When the router can ping the destination successfully but users cannot reach it, an outbound ACL on the router's egress interface is a classic culprit. Router-sourced pings use the router's own IP as the source, which may be permitted by the ACL, while user traffic (sourced from user subnet IPs) is blocked. Always check 'show ip access-lists' and 'show ip interface' (which shows applied ACLs) when the router can reach a destination but users cannot.

flashcards.front: An engineer runs 'show interfaces Gi0/0' and sees 'input errors: 1423, CRC: 1423?
flashcards.back: CRC errors and input errors are typically caused by a duplex mismatch (one side full, other half-duplex) or a bad/damaged cable. They indicate physical or data link layer problems.

flashcards.front: A network engineer runs 'traceroute 8.8.8.8' from a router and observes: hops 1-?
flashcards.back: Traceroute works by sending packets with TTL=1, 2, 3... and expecting ICMP Time Exceeded (type 11) messages back from each router. If routers 4-6 have ACLs or firewall rules blocking outbound ICMP Time Exceeded, they will silently discard the TTL-expired packets without responding — causing '* * *'. The packets are still being forwarded, which is why the destination at hop 7 responds. This is extremely common on internet paths where ISP routers filter ICMP.

nodes.title: VLAN: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on VLAN. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: How many VLANs does the 802.1Q standard support?
flashcards.back: 802.1Q uses a 12-bit VLAN ID field: 2^12 = 4096 values. VLANs 0 and 4095 are reserved, leaving 4094 usable VLANs (1–4094).

flashcards.front: A trunk port carries traffic for VLANs 10, 20, and 30. What technology enables t?
flashcards.back: 802.1Q adds a 4-byte tag to Ethernet frames identifying the VLAN. Trunk ports use this tag so a single link can carry frames from multiple VLANs simultaneously.

flashcards.front: VTP mode 'transparent' is configured on a switch. How does it handle VTP adverti?
flashcards.back: VTP transparent mode forwards VTP advertisements to maintain backward compatibility, but does not synchronize its own VLAN database. It manages its VLANs independently.

flashcards.front: A switch port is configured as an access port in VLAN 30. It receives a frame wi?
flashcards.back: Access ports don't expect 802.1Q tags. Any untagged frame arriving on an access port is automatically associated with the configured access VLAN (VLAN 30 in this case).

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: How many usable host addresses does a /26 subnet provide?
flashcards.back: /26 leaves 6 host bits: 2^6 = 64 total addresses. Subtract 1 network + 1 broadcast = 62 usable hosts.

flashcards.front: What subnet mask corresponds to a /28 prefix length?
flashcards.back: /28 sets 28 bits to 1. The last octet: 11110000 = 240. So the mask is 255.255.255.240.

flashcards.front: On the subnet 192.168.1.64/26, what is the broadcast address?
flashcards.back: /26 = 64 addresses per subnet. Starting at .64, the range ends at .127. The broadcast is 192.168.1.127.

flashcards.front: A company needs to create 5 subnets from 192.168.100.0/24, with each subnet supp?
flashcards.back: A /27 leaves 5 host bits: 2^5 - 2 = 30 usable hosts (≥ 25 ✓). Borrowing 3 bits from a /24 gives 2^3 = 8 subnets (≥ 5 ✓). A /26 fails the subnet count (only 4); /28 fails the host count (only 14); /25 fails the subnet count (only 2).
